name: Temperate rainforest
notes: Cool, very wet coastal forest of giant evergreen conifers (or southern beeches) with a dense fern-and-shrub understory and every trunk draped in moss and lichen; drawn on the Pacific Northwest, Valdivian Chile, New Zealand and Hokkaido.

canopy.name: Coast redwood
canopy.source: Sequoia sempervirens, coast redwood, coastal N California-S Oregon fog belt, tallest tree on Earth 60-115 m — Wikipedia / Gymnosperm Database

canopy.name: Sitka spruce
canopy.source: Picea sitchensis, Sitka spruce, Pacific coast Alaska-N California, temperate rainforest dominant, 50-90 m — Wikipedia / Gymnosperm Database

canopy.name: Hemlock
canopy.source: Tsuga heterophylla, western hemlock, Pacific NW Alaska-California, shade-tolerant climax conifer of coastal rainforest, 40-70 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

canopy.name: Douglas fir
canopy.source: Pseudotsuga menziesii, Douglas fir, western North America, coastal variety in moist conifer forest, 50-90 m deeply furrowed bark — Wikipedia / Gymnosperm Database

canopy.name: Coihue
canopy.source: Nothofagus dombeyi, coihue, evergreen southern beech, Valdivian temperate rainforest of Chile/Argentina, 30-45 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

canopy.name: Rimu
canopy.source: Dacrydium cupressinum, rimu, endemic New Zealand lowland podocarp rainforest, 35-50 m weeping foliage — Wikipedia / NZ Plant Conservation Network

shrub.name: Salal
shrub.source: Gaultheria shallon, salal, Pacific NW coast, dominant evergreen understory shrub of conifer rainforest, 0.5-3 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

shrub.name: Vine maple
shrub.source: Acer circinatum, vine maple, Pacific NW, sprawling understory tree of moist conifer forest, 3-8 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

shrub.name: Devil's club
shrub.source: Oplopanax horridus, devil's club, Alaska-Oregon, wet seeps and stream banks under rainforest canopy, 1-3 m spiny stems, red berries — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

shrub.name: Colihue
shrub.source: Chusquea culeou, colihue, Valdivian rainforest understory of Chile/Argentina, clumping bamboo 3-6 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

shrub.name: Kuril bamboo
shrub.source: Sasa kurilensis, chishima-zasa, Hokkaido, Kurils, Sakhalin & N Honshu, dense dwarf-bamboo understory of cool wet forest, 1-3 m — Wikipedia / Flora of Japan

shrub.name: Silver tree fern
shrub.source: Cyathea dealbata, ponga/silver fern, endemic New Zealand lowland and montane rainforest, trunk 4-10 m, silver frond undersides — Wikipedia / NZPCN

ground.name: Sword fern
ground.source: Polystichum munitum, western sword fern, Pacific NW, dominant evergreen ground fern of redwood/hemlock forest, fronds 0.5-1.5 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

ground.name: Oregon oxalis
ground.source: Oxalis oregana, redwood sorrel, coastal Oregon-California redwood forest floor, dense 5-15 cm carpet — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

ground.name: Stair-step moss
ground.source: Hylocomium splendens, stair-step moss, circumboreal, thick carpets on rainforest floor and logs, 5-15 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Skunk cabbage
ground.source: Lysichiton americanus, western skunk cabbage, Pacific NW swampy rainforest ground, huge leaves 0.5-1.2 m, yellow spathe — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

ground.name: Deer fern
ground.source: Blechnum spicant (Struthiopteris spicant), deer fern, Pacific NW & Atlantic Europe, wet conifer forest floor, 30-70 cm — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

epiphyte.name: Cat-tail moss
epiphyte.source: Isothecium stoloniferum, cat-tail moss, Pacific NW coast, festoons hanging from bigleaf maple and conifer branches, strands 10-50 cm — Wikipedia / E-Flora BC

epiphyte.name: Licorice fern
epiphyte.source: Polypodium glycyrrhiza, licorice fern, Pacific NW, epiphytic on mossy trunks and branches of maple/alder, fronds 15-50 cm — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

epiphyte.name: Old man's beard
epiphyte.source: Usnea longissima, Methuselah's beard lichen, old-growth conifer rainforests of the Pacific NW & Scandinavia, pale hanging strands to 3 m — Wikipedia

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.

associations.name: Sitka spruce-hemlock fog forest
associations.where: coastal fog belt, lower slopes and terraces, very wet
associations.source: Franklin & Dyrness 1973 Natural Vegetation of Oregon and Washington (Picea sitchensis zone)

associations.name: Redwood alluvial flat forest
associations.where: river flats and lower slopes with deep alluvial soil, summer fog
associations.source: Sawyer et al. 2000 Redwood Forest; Franklin & Dyrness 1973

associations.name: Douglas-fir salal slope forest
associations.where: drier south slopes and ridges, well drained, after old fire

associations.name: Coihue-colihue Valdivian forest
associations.where: mid-slopes and valleys of the southern Andes, high rainfall
associations.source: Veblen et al. 1996 Ecology and Biogeography of Nothofagus Forests

associations.name: Rimu-tree fern podocarp forest
associations.where: lowland and low hill country of New Zealand, wet deep soil
